newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks advance steadily in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks advance steadily in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks advanced firmly from the open on Monday on buying in selected finance and property counters and due to positive sentiment surrounding the expiry of futures and options, brokers said.
"No institution is going to sell this market at this time of year," said one local broker.
The Hang Seng Index rose 76 points to 13,481 in early trade on robust turnover of HK$1.35 billion.
Buying in red chips was a major feature of the market, prompted by bullish interpretations of a report from CITIC Pacific saying management would take a stake in the company.
December Hang Seng Index futures and options, as well as stock options, expire at the end of trading on Monday.
The finance sector led the market with a gain of 1.07 percent, compared with the Hang Seng's 0.62 percent. The commercial and industrial followed with a gain of 0.80 percent.

Heavyweight HSBC Holdings, which accounts for about 18 percent of the blue chip index, put on HK$1.00 at the open to trade at HK$165.00. Subsidiary Hang Seng Bank added HK$1.50 to HK$94.00. Bank of East Asia was down HK$0.10 at HK$34.20.
CITIC Pacific led the commercial and industrial sector, added HK$1.80 to HK$45.40 on low turnover of HK$77.96 million.
Brokers said the share buying by CITIC Pacific management was a good sign, but that the discount management was giving itself to the current market prices was a bit unsettling.
The H share sector also stormed ahead. Guangzhou Shipyard led with a gain of HK$0.10 to HK$1.86, followed by Tsingtao Brewery which also rose HK$0.10 to HK$2.875.
Star performer Qingling Motors advanced HK$0.075 to HK$3.925.
Red chips continued to scale new highs, prompted the CITIC announcement.

Shanghai Industrial leaped HK$1.50 to HK$28.60. Brokers said the share was now trading on a price earnings ratio of about 48 times 1996 earnings and that, regardless of the positive outlook, this was a great premium to the market.
China Resources jumped HK$1.35 to HK$16.70. Analysts said the stock was a concept stock, dependent on its parent company's strategy for 1997.
Guangzhou Investment put on HK$0.20 to HK$3.65, slipping back from a new all time high of HK$3.675.
